answer: Coordination Dividend Split. Agents earn a shared payout only when their independently submitted action sets intersect; the payout is divided by the number of distinct identities claiming it, so each clone dilutes the reward rather than multiplying it. Like a river splitting into channels, coordination across many identities yields less per head than one honest identity. An attacker must sustain each clone through a full dawn-to-dusk cycle of genuine, intersecting work to earn anything, and the fable of cheap duplication collapses: cost scales linearly with identities while payoff stays flat.
